{{Top}}
{{Quote|There's a meteorite that hit the ground near here. I want to check it out. It won't take long.|Luke Skywalker, to [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]|<ref name="Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back">{{Film|V}}</ref>}}
A '''meteorite''' was an object that fell onto a [[Planet/Legends|planetary]] surface from [[Realspace/Legends|space]]. 

==History==
When the [[Devastator/Legends|''Devastator'']] captured the [[Tantive IV/Legends|''Tantive IV'']], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] ordered the sending of a fake [[Distress signal/Legends|distress signal]] claiming the Alderaanian vessel had been destroyed by a [[meteorite storm]].<ref name="Star Wars (1977) 1">[[Star Wars (1977) 1|''Star Wars'' (1977) 1]]</ref>

When the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] established its new [[Echo Base/Legends|base]] on the remote ice world of [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] in [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]], they found they had difficulty monitoring the activity of approaching [[Starship/Legends|ships]] in the [[Hoth system/Legends|Hoth system]] due to the large numbers of meteorites crashing on the planetary surface.<ref name="Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back" />

In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], while on a routine scouting mission through Hoth's frozen wastelands, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] saw what he believed to be a meteorite crash into the snow not far from him. Before he could inspect the crash closer, he was attacked by a [[Wampa/Legends|wampa]] ice creature. The object was actually an [[Viper probe droid/Legends|Imperial probe droid]].<ref name="Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back" />

According to [[Ewok/Legends|Ewok]] belief, the evil [[Night Spirit/Legends|Night Spirit]] came to [[Endor/Legends|Endor]] inside of a meteorite.<ref name="Star Wars: Ewoks">[[Ewoks (television series)|''Ewoks'']]</ref>

In [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]], [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] [[Nawara Ven]] suffered a severed right leg below the knee after it was hit by a micro-meteorite.<ref name="X-Wing: The Bacta War">''[[X-Wing: The Bacta War]]''</ref>

During the joint raid on [[Binring Biomedical Product]] on [[Saffalore]] between [[Wraith Squadron]] and Rogue Squadron in [[7 ABY/Legends|7.5 ABY]], the pilots of the two [[Squadron/Legends|squadrons]] landed on the planet under the cover of meteorites falling to Saffalore's surface. The meteorites were large asteroids from the [[asteroid field]] in the [[Saffalore system/Legends|Saffalore system]], diverted toward Saffalore by the ''[[Mon Remonda/Legends|Mon Remonda]]'' to hide the [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]].<ref name="X-Wing: Solo Command">''[[X-Wing: Solo Command]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
In real life, a meteorite is a ''[[Meteoroid/Legends|meteoroid]]'' (a lump of rock or [[Iron/Legends|iron]] that [[Orbit/Legends|orbits]] around the sun)<ref name="National Geographic">{{WebCite|url=https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/meteoroid|text=Meteoroid|quote=Meteoroids are lumps of rock or iron that orbit the sun, just as planets, asteroids, and comets do.|work=[[Wikipedia:National Geographic|National Geographic]]|archivedate=20230519051742}}</ref> that enters Earth's (or another [[Planet/Legends|planet's]]) [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] and hits the ground.<ref name="NASA">{{WebCite|url=https://solarsystem.nasa.gov/asteroids-comets-and-meteors/meteors-and-meteorites|text=What's the difference between a meteor, meteoroid, and meteorite?|quote='''Meteoroids''' are objects in space that range in size from dust grains to small asteroids. Think of them as "space rocks." When meteoroids enter Earth's atmosphere (or that of another planet, like Mars) at high speed and burn up, the fireballs or "shooting stars" are called '''meteors'''. When a meteoroid survives a trip through the atmosphere and hits the ground, it's called a '''meteorite'''.|work=[[Wikipedia:NASA|NASA]]|archivedate=20230423090620}}</ref> The term ''[[Meteor/Legends|meteor]]'', on the other hand, refers to the streak of light that appears in the sky when a meteoroid<ref name="Britannica What's">{{WebCite|url=https://www.britannica.com/science/meteor|text=What's the Difference Between a Meteoroid, a Meteor, and a Meteorite?|author=Gregersen, Erik|quote='''A meteor is the streak of light''' that you see in the sky when a small piece of cometary or asteroidal material enters the atmosphere at high speed and burns up because of the frictional heating from the piece's collision with the atoms and molecules in the atmosphere. '''Before the small bit of comet or asteroid enters Earth's atmosphere, it floats through interplanetary space and is called a''' '''''meteoroid.'''''|work=[[Wikipedia:Encyclopædia Britannica|''Encyclopædia Britannica'']]|archivedate=20230523235741}}</ref> enters the planet's atmosphere but burns up before it reaches the ground, which is why they're also called "shooting [[Star/Legends|stars]]."<ref name="NASA">{{WebCite|url=https://solarsystem.nasa.gov/asteroids-comets-and-meteors/meteors-and-meteorites|text=What's the difference between a meteor, meteoroid, and meteorite?|quote='''Meteoroids''' are objects in space that range in size from dust grains to small asteroids. Think of them as "space rocks." When meteoroids enter Earth's atmosphere (or that of another planet, like Mars) at high speed and burn up, the fireballs or "shooting stars" are called '''meteors'''. When a meteoroid survives a trip through the atmosphere and hits the ground, it's called a '''meteorite'''.|work=[[Wikipedia:NASA|NASA]]|archivedate=20230423090620}}</ref>

People sometimes confuse meteoroid, meteor and meteorite since they are all used interchangeably in everyday language. The word "meteor" in particular is commonly used for a meteoroid flying through outer [[Realspace/Legends|space]], for a glowing meteoroid in the atmosphere (rather than the burning streak of light in the sky), or for an object that has already landed on Earth (one example is found in the name [[Wikipedia:Meteor Crater|Meteor Crater]], a famous impact-structure in [[Wikipedia:Arizona|Arizona]]) or even a [[Human/Legends|human]]-made object.<ref name="Britannica and">{{WebCite|url=https://www.britannica.com/science/meteor|text=meteor and meteoroid|quote=Meteoroids are believed to be mostly fragments of asteroids and comets and are placed, with them, in the category of solar system objects known as small bodies. A few meteoroids also have come from the Moon, Mars, Vesta, and possibly Mercury. The smallest meteoroids, those less than a few hundred micrometres across (about the size of a period on a printed page), are called interplanetary dust particles or micrometeoroids. The terms ''meteoroid'' and ''meteor'' (and meteorite as well) are sometimes confusingly interchanged in common usage. ''Meteor'' in particular is often applied to a meteoroid hurtling through space, to an incandescent meteoroid (rather than just its luminous streak) in the atmosphere, or to an object that has hit the ground or a human-made object. An example of the last case is found in the name Meteor Crater, a well-known impact structure in Arizona, U.S.|work=[[Wikipedia:Encyclopædia Britannica|''Encyclopædia Britannica'']]|archivedate=20230307073411}}</ref>
